correctness.rationale: For every distinct-prime p and ell, q=ell^r, zero-frequency sums of p q-roots cannot vanish by the explicit cyclotomic coefficient argument; for any nonzero frequency, irreducibility of Phi_p over Q(zeta_q) means a vanishing Fourier coefficient forces a constant product row; two different constant shifts imply a common prime-order and q-order multiplier, hence both input words constant. The three support sets and unique shift follow, and independent phase-normalized pairs count exactly 1, p(q^(p-1)-1), q^(2p-2)-1-p(q^(p-1)-1). Direct independent enumeration verified all pairs for five small parameter cases, largest 65536. All cases p=2 and r>=1 are covered; computations supplement an all-parameter algebraic proof.

value.rationale: Determines a complete natural support spectrum, not a bound: all p^2 time-frequency bins are nonzero except for at most one p-1-frequency line unless both words are constant. The exact phase-normalized multiplicities and complete support geometry hold for infinitely many cyclic dimensions and arbitrary coprime prime-power phase alphabets. This is motivated by finite-alphabet time-frequency waveform zero design and quantifies a strong alphabet-induced gap absent from unrestricted phase-only models. The q composite counterexample sharply explains the arithmetic restriction. It is neither an arbitrary single finite case nor a routine numerical recomputation.
